arxiv-2208-04238.title: POSET-RL: Phase ordering for Optimizing Size and Execution Time using Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2208-04238.creator: Shalini Jain 1 , Yashas Andaluri 2 , S. VenkataKeerthy 3 and Ramakrishna Upadrasta 4
arxiv-2208-04238.description: Abstract The ever increasing memory requirements of several applications has led to increased demands which might not be met by embedded devices. Constraining the usage of memory in such cases is of paramount importance. It is important that such code size improvements should not have a negative impact on the runtime.

arxiv-2212-10476.title: Pierre Auger Observatory and Super Heavy Dark Matter
arxiv-2212-10476.creator: \firstname Roberto \lastname Aloisio \fnsep \lastname for the Pierre Auger Collaboration \fnsep
arxiv-2212-10476.description: Abstract We briefly discuss the connection of the Pierre Auger Observatory data with a large class of dark matter models based on the early universe generation of super heavy particles, their role in the solution of the dark matter problem, highlighting the remarkable constraining capabilities of the Auger observations.

arxiv-2305-12897.creator: Henning Bruhn, Raphael Steck
arxiv-2305-12897.description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Henning Bruhn, Raphael Steck. We show that walls of size at least 6 × 4 6\times 4 do not have the edge-Erdős-Pósa property. 1
Introduction

The Erdős-Pósa property provides a duality between packing and covering in graphs.

arxiv-2503-14424.title: Identifying Materials-Level Sources of Performance Variation in Superconducting Transmon Qubits
arxiv-2503-14424.creator: Akshay A. Murthy ∗, Mustafa Bal, Michael J. Bedzyk, Hilal Cansizoglu, Randall K. Chan, Venkat Chandrasekhar, Francesco Crisa, Amlan Datta, Yanpei Deng, Celeo D. Matute Diaz, Vinayak P. Dravid, David A. Garcia-Wetten, Sabrina Garattoni, Sunil Ghimire, Dominic P. Goronzy, Sebastian E. de Graaf, Sam Ha
arxiv-2503-14424.description: Abstract The Superconducting Materials and Systems (SQMS) Center, a DOE National Quantum Information Science Research Center, has conducted a comprehensive and coordinated study using superconducting transmon qubit chips with known performance metrics to identify the underlying materials-level sources of device-to-device performance variation.

arxiv-2512-02726.title: AuditCopilot: Leveraging LLMs for Fraud Detection in Double-Entry Bookkeeping
arxiv-2512-02726.creator: Md Abdul Kadir, Sai Suresh Macharla Vasu, Sidharth S. Nair, Daniel Sonntag
arxiv-2512-02726.description: Abstract Auditors rely on Journal Entry Tests (JETs) to detect anomalies in tax-related ledger records, but rule-based methods generate overwhelming false positives and struggle with subtle irregularities. We investigate whether large language models (LLMs) can serve as anomaly detectors in double-entry bookkeeping.

arxiv-2601-04288.title: Human-in-the-Loop Testing of AI Agents for Air Traffic Control with a Regulated Assessment Framework
arxiv-2601-04288.creator: Ben Carvell and Marc Thomas, Andrew Pace and Christopher Dorney, George De Ath, Richard Everson, Nick Pepper and Adam Keane, Samuel Tomlinson and Richard Cannon
arxiv-2601-04288.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Ben Carvell and Marc Thomas, Andrew Pace and Christopher Dorney, George De Ath, Richard Everson, Nick Pepper and Adam Keane, Samuel Tomlinson and Richard Cannon. We present a rigorous, human-in-the-loop evaluation framework for assessing the performance of AI agents on the task of Air Traffic Control, grounded in a regulator-certified simulator-based curriculum used for training and testing real-world trainee controllers.

pmc-12576962.title: Topographic Variation in Human Neurotransmitter Receptor Densities Explains Differences in Intracranial EEG Spectra
pmc-12576962.creator: U. M. Stoof, K. J. Friston, M. Tisdall, G. K. Cooray, R. E. Rosch
pmc-12576962.description: Brain function and its failures arise from dynamical patterns of neuronal activity shaped by synaptic neurotransmission. Both neurotransmitter receptor expression and neuronal population dynamics show a remarkable regional variability across the human cortex. We leverage this functional specialisation to characterise the relationship between receptor architectonics and electrophysiological signals.

pmc-12604207.title: Performance of clinical prediction models for chronic kidney disease among people with diabetes: external validation using the Canadian Primary Care Sentinel Surveillance Network (CPCSSN)
pmc-12604207.creator: Jason E. Black, David JT. Campbell, Paul E. Ronksley, Kerry A. McBrien, Tyler S. Williamson
pmc-12604207.description: BackgroundSeveral clinical prediction models that predict the risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD) in people with diabetes have been developed; however, these models lack external validation demonstrating accurate predictions in Canadian primary care. We externally validated existing clinical prediction models for CKD in Canadian primary care data, overall and across subgroups defined by sex/gender, age, comorbidities, and neighbourhood-level deprivation.

pmc-12639966.title: Enhanced recovery after surgery versus conventional approach in peptic perforation- a Randomized Controlled Trial- “ERASE trial”
pmc-12639966.creator: Swastik Sourav Mishra, Tushar Subhadarshan Mishra, Pankaj Kumar, Pradeep Kumar Singh, Prakash Kumar Sasmal, Upendra Hansda, Shritosh Kumar, Mahesh Kumar Sethi
pmc-12639966.description: BackgroundImplementing Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocol in elective surgeries has improved outcomes. Evidence for a similar role in emergency surgeries must be explored, particularly in patients with peptic perforation. This research aims to study the safety and efficacy of ERAS in patients undergoing surgery for peptic perforation peritonitis.

pmc-12751372.title: The Effect of Methylene Blue on Sublingual Microcirculation in Patients with Septic Shock: A Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-12751372.creator: Cuicui Dong, Jiaqi Zhu, Hang Ni, Yanfang Chen, Benjia Chen, Mengqin Zhang, Ke Cui, Sheng Zhang, Yongpo Jiang, Yinghe Xu
pmc-12751372.description: BackgroundMethylene blue (MB) has been proposed as an adjunctive therapy in the early management of septic shock; however, its effects on microcirculatory function remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate whether MB infusion improves sublingual microcirculatory parameters in patients with septic shock.

pmc-12988127.title: Twisted atomic magnetic tunnel junctions with multiple nonvolatile states
pmc-12988127.creator: Yuliang Chen, Kartik Samanta, Alexander J. Healey, Chi Fang, Haojie Zhang, Naafis A. Shahed, David A. Broadway, Arthur Ernst, Evgeny Y. Tsymbal, Stuart S. P. Parkin
pmc-12988127.description: Magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs), a key spintronic device, have shown rapid development recently using two-dimensional (2D) magnets. In particular, MTJs formed from twisted 2D antiferromagnets (AFMs) push nonvolatile magnetic information storage to the atomic limit. Here we demonstrate 2D twisted MTJs with multiple distinct nonvolatile states.

pmc-13062662.title: Effect of weight reduction on liver volume in living liver donors with steatosis: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13062662.creator: Kwangpyo Hong, Kwang-Woong Lee, Su young Hong, Sola Lee, Hyun Hwa Choi, Jiyoung Kim, Jaewon Lee, Jae-Yoon Kim, Jeong-Moo Lee, Suk Kyun Hong, YoungRok Choi
pmc-13062662.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeWeight reduction (WR) can reduce liver volume, affecting the graft-to-recipient weight ratio (GRWR). This study aimed to evaluate the decrease in liver volume after WR and analyze risk factors affecting liver volume reduction in potential liver donors with steatosis.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed data of 147 potential liver donors with steatosis who participated in a WR program prior to liver transplantation between January 2016 and December 2021. Total liver volume (TLV) was measured using CT and MRI.

pmc-13316383.title: Point-of-care diagnostics are central to acute medicine delivery
pmc-13316383.creator: Catherine Atkin, Murali Veerabahu, Daniel Lasserson, Sarb Clare
pmc-13316383.description: Point-of-care diagnostics deliver rapid, actionable results to aid in clinical decision making for patients with acute illness. Ranging from in vitro diagnostics, such as high-sensitivity troponin, to point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS), incorporating point-of-care diagnostics into clinical care offers accelerated decision making and streamlined assessment pathways.

pmc-13352769.title: Integrative expression profiling and comparative bioinformatics analysis of ALDH7A1 in chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) under salt and ABA treatments
pmc-13352769.creator: Serap Demirel, Melike İncetekin, Ahmet Say, Hamdi Özaktan, Kahraman Gürcan, Fatih Demirel
pmc-13352769.description: BackgroundSoil salinity and abscisic acid (ABA)-related signaling are major constraints affecting chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) productivity by promoting oxidative stress and aldehyde accumulation. Aldehyde dehydrogenases (ALDHs), particularly members of the ALDH7 family, are involved in aldehyde detoxification and redox homeostasis under adverse conditions.

pmc-13367707.title: Addressing historical biases and the limits of biomedical commodities in vector-borne disease control in Africa
pmc-13367707.creator: Jennifer S. Lord, Ellie Sherrard-Smith, Antoine Sanou, Fredros Okumu
pmc-13367707.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In this essay, we describe efforts to curtail the spread of vector-borne infections and how these efforts are entangled in the causes and consequences of the destruction of life, and the ecosystems which support life, on our planet. Using examples from malaria and sleeping sickness, we show how current efforts to control vector-borne diseases reflect the Western logic of a highly compartmentalized, hierarchical approach, dominated by biomedicine and commoditized interventions.

pmc-13384472.title: Data-Driven Healthy China Pathway: Evolution, Framework, and Global Implications of National Digital Health Strategic Planning
pmc-13384472.creator: Jialin Liu, Siru Liu, Ivan Steenstra
pmc-13384472.description: Amid accelerating digital health transformation, China has developed a centrally coordinated data-driven healthy China pathway. This viewpoint conceptualizes this pathway as a hybrid continuous planning framework (HCPF) that links long-term strategic direction with short-cycle tactical adaptation. China’s strategy has progressed through 3 overlapping periods: infrastructure-oriented periodic planning (2015-2018), emergency-driven digital acceleration (2019-2021), and institutionalized continuous planning (2022-2025).

pmc-13471499.title: Prenatal monitoring in primary health care: a design science research-based approach to FHIR interoperability
pmc-13471499.creator: Renata D Braga, Plinio S Leitao-Junior, Suse B Castilho, Dandra A Souza, Lismary B Oliveira, Michael L D Oliveira, Luiselena L Esmeraldo, Carlos A G Tibiriçá, Diana F Guimarães, Aline R Nogueira, Livia M Vilela, Rejane F Ribeiro-Rotta, Fabio N Lucena, Juliana P Souza-Zinader
pmc-13471499.description: BackgroundThis research addresses the development and validation of an information model for pregnancy monitoring that, through the Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) specification, seeks to promote interoperability for the quality of prenatal care by multidisciplinary teams in Brazilian primary healthcare contexts.

pmc-13488060.title: Incidental cystic pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasm and differential diagnosis
pmc-13488060.creator: Daniel Martin, Eric R Taylor, Enas Abdallah, Mintallah Haider, Keith Ferguson, Daniel Jeong, Sebastian Feuerlein, James R Costello
pmc-13488060.description: Pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (panNENs) are tumors derived from pancreatic precursor cells with neuroendocrine differentiation. They display characteristic biologic, histopathologic, and functional features which define their classification along a spectrum ranging from well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (panNETs) to poorly differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine carcinomas (panNECs).

uslaw-usc-t10-s7138.title: 10 U.S.C. § 7138 — Regular Army: reenlistment after service as an officer
uslaw-usc-t10-s7138.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s7138.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part II (Personnel); Chapter 713 (Enlistments). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Any former enlisted member of the Regular Army who has served on active duty as an officer of the Army, or who was discharged as an enlisted member to accept an appointment as an officer of the Army, is entitled to be reenlisted.

uslaw-usc-t12-s4703a.title: 12 U.S.C. § 4703a — Capital investments for neighborhoods disproportionately impacted by the COVID–19 pandemic
uslaw-usc-t12-s4703a.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t12-s4703a.description: United States Code, Title 12 (Banks And Banking); Chapter 47 (Community Development Banking); Subchapter I (Community Development Banking And Financial Institutions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Definitions In this section— (1) the term “bank holding company” has the meaning given the term in section 1841 of this title; (2) the term “eligible institution” means any low- and moderate-income community financial institution.
